text:
Afternoon's playing out just the way it was drawn up: sunny and quiet, sitting right around 40, which is a touch milder than the morning felt. That's about where we top out, and with the sun setting a little after 4:15, it cools off quickly once it dips. Tonight stays partly cloudy and cold, down to around 23, so expect frost on the windshield first thing Thursday.

Thanksgiving itself starts dry, with clouds thickening through the day and a high in the low 40s. The models disagree a bit on just how mild, but I'd bet on low 40s. The rain holds off until the evening, with the first drops likely between 9 and midnight. Because the air is so dry and cold ahead of it, it could start as a brief glaze of ice before warming up. Use caution on bridges and elevated surfaces late Thursday. It then turns to plain rain overnight, with a half to three quarters of an inch by Friday morning and more waves of rain through Friday.

If you're traveling or hosting, plan to be home and settled by 9 Thursday night.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure will remain in control today, keeping quiet weather in place. Temperatures will top out in the upper 30s to lower 40s, which is right around seasonal normals for this time of year. Temperatures will continue to moderate slightly on Thursday as high pressure shifts east of the area and return southerly flow develops. In the wake of the departing high pressure, a low pressure system will travel northward through the eastern United States, sending a wave of precipitation northward into our forecast area. Precipitation onset across our CWA is generally expected between 9 PM Thursday and midnight Thursday night. Temperatures ahead of the system on Thursday will have risen to above freezing for all but the highest elevations in our CWA. With dry air in place ahead of the system, wet-bulb cooling at the onset and localized northeasterly flow will bring temperatures to near or just below freezing across localized portions of the area. It will take some time to saturate through the low levels, so despite soundings that may be favorable for freezing rain at the onset, ice accumulations will be limited. The best window for freezing rain and accumulated ice will occur between 8 PM and 4 AM Thursday night/Friday morning. Total ice amounts are forecast to range from a glaze up to a tench of an inch across the northern Saint Lawrence Valley, eastern Adirondacks, and higher elevations of the Greens and northeastern Vermont. Outside of these areas, rain will be the predominant precipitation type throughout the event. Impacts from the initial ice will be limited however, as warming temperatures Friday morning will allow for a transition to a cold rain by daybreak for most areas. In addition, surfaces will start off above freezing Thursday, which will also limit accumulations. However, use caution if you have travel plans late Thursday and Thursday night, especially over elevated surfaces and bridges. KEY MESSAGE 2: Aside from a brief period of localized freezing rain, some localized strong winds are also expected. The core of an easterly 70 to 80 knot low level jet will move northward through our forecast area. The jet will move through at the same time as a wave of rain. The stabilizing effect of the rain on the low levels will prevent the strongest winds from mixing down to the valleys, though some breezy conditions are anticipated. However, higher elevations (2000 ft+) of the southern Greens and Essex County NY will see a period of strong winds with gusts reaching 35 to 55 mph Thursday night. Summits could gust in excess of 60 mph. These winds could be preceded by some light ice accumulations in the higher elevations, though this would mainly be limited to elevations above 2500 ft. By sunrise Friday morning, winds will start to diminish and precipitation type will be fully a cold rain across the forecast area. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Wednesday! The busy travel day today ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday looks quiet and a bit warmer with temperatures in the mid to upper 30s and lower 40s for Wednesday afternoon. The day features a good deal of sunshine. Black Friday will see any mountain mixed precipitation transition into mainly rain, and rain could be heavier at times, especially through the morning hours and becoming a bit more scattered by Friday evening and night. The other big component to this system looks to be the wind. That is why we have gone ahead and issued a First Alert Weather Day for Friday. The real bullseye for the wind will be right along the western slopes of the mountains, where they could see gusts upwards of 40-60 MPH. This could be enough to result in scattered power outages Friday. Intensity will vary widely over short distances. Ridgelines and communities on or near the western mountain slopes again could see a window of gusts as high as 40 to 60 mph early Friday. Conditions have to come together in the right way to see the higher end gusts make it to the ground. We usually see wind gusts intensify when rain slows down or stops. Gusts will be much less intense away from the western slopes. Some areas won’t see much wind at all. The strongest gusts will likely occur early Friday morning, especially if there is a lull in precipitation. Wind will trend lighter through the morning and into Friday afternoon. Saturday looks drier overall, but there could still be a few scattered showers and mountain snow showers from time to time. Temperatures are again in the low to mid 40s. Winds look to be calmer through the day Saturday. By Sunday, most of us are back to dry, but cloudy conditions as temperatures continue to warm by a few degrees and we head back towards the mid and upper 40s and lower 50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-24T23:41:00Z — same caveat): Rain, wind, some ice arrives late Thanksgiving into Friday — The quiet but chilly weather continues Wednesday. Expect a mostly sunny sky, with highs in the upper 30s to near 40. Thanksgiving starts dry, with some sun, before clouds thicken up by afternoon. A coastal low sends in steady rain by evening or overnight, which may start as an icy mix in the northern mountains. Highs reach the low 40s. Strong downslope wind will cause issues Thursday night into Friday morning. Bennington County is where the most outages will be, with 70 mph gust potential. Some will also occur in eastern Rutland and Addison counties. By daytime Friday, less wind. Expect a cloudy sky with scattered rain showers through the morning and afternoon. A few snowflakes may mix in for the mountains, especially late. This weekend brings lingering showers of rain and mountain snow (especially Saturday), lots of clouds and a mild feel. Highs reach the 40s to around 50.
